category_title: Students who use physical and verbal resistance to negotiate classroom autonomy
scenario_title: Negotiating schedule to continue persuasive writing
minimal_context: The student is participating in a class meeting after lunch to transition to a planned math activity, but wants to continue writing their opinions about race.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Welcome back from lunch and recess. It is time to transition to our planned math activity.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: We should keep writing. We can do math tomorrow. Talking about race is important. I might forget what I want to say.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to follow the schedule we have set for today.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: What if we took turns? So, like, people that want to write can. People who want to do math, can.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We all need to do the same activity right now. Please get ready for math.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, I'm going to be super mad if I can't finish my writing. I will just be here and not do anything! (Lies down on the floor)

STUDENT: Well, I'm going to be super mad if I can't finish my writing. I will just be here and not do anything! (Lies down on the floor)
